The table below summarizes the processes that dominate radiation and advection fog events. A key feature of advection fog events is that the boundary layer can tolerate relatively high wind speeds while still maintaining the fog event. In contrast, radiation fog events are normally associated with boundary layer winds less than five knots because windier conditions would cause entrainment of drier air aloft and would mix out the saturated conditions closer to the surface.
Radiation and Advection Fog Characteristics
This table deals with the different characteristics of both radiation and advection fog.
Note: The delineation between fog types is not always straightforward because over time, fog that is formed primarily by radiative processes may be supported by dynamic or advective processes,

Terminal Aerodrome Forecast

Terminal Aerodrome Forecasts, also known as Aerodrome Forecasts, are prepared by Aerodrome Forecast Office (AFO). 

The definition of terminal is an area within five 8 km of the center of an airport’s runway complex.

A TAF will consist of expected meteorological conditions significant to aviation at the airport (terminal) for a specified time period.

TAFs are a critical element of aviation weather services because they are a key product in decisions on aircraft movement.

Used in combination with fog (FG), showers (SH), and thunderstorms (TS)

Less stringent operational impacts on users than PROB30 groups

Vicinity =  A donut-shaped area between circles with radii of 5 and
10 SM from the center of the runway complex of an airport.
slides.notes:
--When the Forecaster feels there is a less than 50% chance for significant weather within the terminal aerodrome…but still wants to make the user aware of the potential for fog, showers, or thunderstorms w/in the airfield…he/she may chose to include a Vicinity in the TAF.

--The use of VC has less stringent operational impact on the users than PROB30 or TEMPO. Basically, with a PROB30 or TEMPO…the user has to treat this as the prevailing condition…meaning Commercial airlines might add extra fuel for an alternate destination…or for the GA Pilot, this could mean you are grounded depending on your flight credentials and/or aircraft capabilities.
 
--What does it mean if you, the TAF user, see a VC or a CB in the TAF? Even though the prevailing wx conditions are not show stoppers, the user needs to be pro-active and ask himself “what will I do if I encounter TS within the vicinity of the Airfield? Will this cause me significant problems…or can I (and my aircraft) handle this? 

--As for CB…the user will need to treat this as a heads up that the atmosphere they are flying into/out of is unstable…which could mean turbulence…or even an isolated thunderstorm or two might pop up…but the forecaster confidence is low…and if Tstorms do develop, they will be short-lived and minimal in coverage.

Roles and responsibilities of the WAFS

The World Area Forecast System (WAFS) is a program developed by ICAO and WMO to improve the quality and consistency of en-route guidance provided for international aircraft operations
Services meet Annex 3 provisions of the ICAO Convention on Civil Aviation (Meteorological Services for International Air Navigation)

Global upper-air wind/temperature and humidity forecasts, and global significant weather (SIGWX) forecasts, in digital format, are provided by two World Area Forecast Centres (WAFCs):
WAFC London (United Kingdom)
WAFC Washington (United States of America)

WAFC London (Met Office, Exeter, UK) is responsible for satellite data broadcasts to:
Europe

WAFC Washington (Aviation Weather Centre, Kansas City, USA) is responsible for satellite data broadcasts to:

The Atlantic

Light turbulence - briefly causes slight, erratic changes in altitude and/or attitude.

Safety: Wake vortex encounters are capable of compromising aircraft safety
Airport capacity: traffic at many airports limited by wake vortex separation requirements
S-Wake: comprehensive European program focussing on different aspects of WV (experimental, CFD modelling, meteorology)
30/9/05 incident at Barcelona in clear, calm conditions. B737 following A310 encountered wake vortices turbulence on climb-out.

All aircraft produce wake turbulence. 
Wake vortices are formed any time an airfoil is producing lift. The pressure differential across the wing triggers the rollup of the airflow aft of the wing resulting in swirling air masses trailing downstream of the wingtips. 
Viewed from behind the generating aircraft, the left vortex rotates clockwise and the right vortex rotates counterclockwise. 
The strength of the vortex depends primarily on aircraft weight and configuration. 
The strongest vortices are produced by heavy aircraft, flying slowly, in a clean configuration. 
While there have been rare instances where wake turbulence caused structural damage, the greatest hazard is induced roll and yaw. 
This is especially dangerous during takeoff and landing when there is little altitude for recovery. 
Helicopters also make wake turbulence

The primary purpose of SIGMET and AIRMET is for in-flight service, which requires timely transmission of the SIGMET and, where available, AIRMET messages to pilots by the ATS units and/or through VOLMET and D-VOLMET 

Airlines are the main users of the SIGMET and AIRMET information 

SIGMET and AIRMET is also used for the flight planning

SIGMET and AIRMET information is issued by the MWO in order to provide timely warning for the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified en-route weather phenomena, affecting the safety of the flight operations in the MWO’s area of responsibility. SIGMET and AIRMET provides information concerning the location, extent, intensity and expected evolution of the specified phenomena

SIGMET for en-route weather phenomena other than volcanic ash or tropical cyclones (WS SIGMET )

SIGMET for volcanic ash (VA SIGMET) (to be referred also as WV SIGMET) 

SIGMET for tropical cyclones (TC SIGMET)

WMO Header : T1T2A1A2ii CCCC YYGGgg 
The group T1T2A1A2ii is the bulletin identification for the SIGMET message. It is constructed in the following way: 
T1T2 	Data type designator
	WA – for AIRMET  
	WS – for SIGMET 
	WC – for SIGMET for tropical cyclone (not required in the EUR Region) 
	WV – for SIGMET for volcanic ash 	
A1A2 	Country or territory designators
ii 	Bulletin number Assigned on national level 	
CCCC is the ICAO location indicator of the communication centre disseminating the message (could be the same as the MWO). 
YYGGgg is the date/time group, where YY is the date and GGgg is the time in hours and minutes UTC, of the transmission of the SIGMET
Format of the meteorological part of SIGMET messages for weather phenomena other than VA

SIGMET shall be issued only: 
thunderstorms – if they are OBSC, EMBD, FRQ or SQL with or without hail; 

turbulence – only SEV 

icing – only SEV with or without FZRA 

mountain waves – only SEV 

dust storm – only HVY 

sand storm – only HVY 

radioactive cloud – RDOACT CLD

Significant Weather Potentially Hazardous To All Aircraft
Max Forecast Period Is 4 Hours
Time of issuance of the SIGMET should be not more than 4 hours before the expected time of occurrence of the phenomenon
Only one WX  phenomena per SIGMET massage

If, during the validity period of a SIGMET, the phenomenon for which the SIGMET had been issued is no longer occurring or no longer expected, this SIGMET should be cancelled by the issuing MWO. 
The cancellation is done by issuing the same type of SIGMET with the following structure: 
WMO heading with the same data type designator; 
First line, including the next sequence number followed by a new validity period, and 
Second line, which contains the location indicator and name of the FIR or CTA, the combination CNL SIGMET, followed by the sequential number of the original SIGMET and its validity period.

Examples: 
Cancellation of a SIGWX SIGMET with the following first line 
WSXY31 YUSO 101200 
YUDD SIGMET 5 VALID 101200/101600 YUSO- 
YUDD SHANLON FIR … 
Cancellation SIGMET: 
WSXY31 YUSO 101430 
YUDD SIGMET 6 VALID 101430/101600 YUSO-

AIRMET is issued for a flight information region (FIR); where necessary, the FIR should be divided in sub-areas and separate AIRMET issued for each sub-area. 

AIRMET messages should be kept short and clear, without additional descriptive text other than that prescribed in Annex 3. 

After issuing an AIRMET, the MWO should maintain watch over the evolution of the phenomenon for which the AIRMET has been issued and issue a new updated AIRMET when necessary

Obscured (OBSC) indicates that the TS is obscured by haze or smoke or cannot be readily seen due to darkness 
Embedded (EMBD) – indicates that the TS is embedded within cloud layers and cannot be readily recognized 
Frequent (FRQ) indicates an area of TS within which there is little or no separation between adjacent TS with a maximum spatial coverage greater than 75% of the area affected, or forecasts to be affected, by the phenomenon (at a fixed time or during the period of validity) 
Squall line (SQL) indicates TS along a line with little or no space between individual clouds 
Severe (SEV) turbulence (TURB) refers only to: 
- low-level turbulence associated with strong surface winds;
- rotor streaming; 
- turbulence whether in cloud or not in cloud (CAT) near to jet streams. 
A mountain wave (MTW) is considered:
	- severe – whenever an accompanying downdraft of 3.0 m/s or more and/or severe turbulence is observed or forecasted.

GAP WINDS הן רוחות במפלס גובה נמוך הקשורות לתצורות  טופוגרפיות כגון ואדיות גאיות או מיצרים.
הן יכולות לנשב לאורך  מאות מטרים עד מאות קילומטרים ובמצבים קיצוניים להגיע לעוצמה של מעל ל 50 קשר. 
מפלס הרוח (אנכי) די רדוד ונע בטווח שבין כמה מאות לכמה אלפי רגל מעל פני השטח, עם גזירות רוח חזקות בשוליים העליונים והתחתונים של "הזרם".
GAP WINDS בד"כ חזקות יותר כאשר מתרחשת ירידת לחץ מעבר למכשול הטופוגרפי, על אף שקיים סוג אחר של רוח תיעול שאינו תלוי בגרדיינט.

טיסות מבצעיות דורשות מידע מדויק על רוחות בגובה נמוך. 
עוצמת הרוח יכול לנוע בטווח שבין 20-60 קשר עם גזירות רוח חזקות בשולי "הזרם" (לאורכו ולרוחבו) שיכולים ליצור חתחותים חמורים ולפיכך להשפיע מאוד על מבצעים צבאיים.

נהוג להסביר את מנגנון  ה-GAP WIND באמצעות מה שמכונה "צינור וונטורי", בו הרוחות החזקות מנשבות בחלק הצר של הזרימה, על אף שלמעשה רוחות חזקות יותר מנשבות באזור היציאה "מהצינור". בנוסף מנגנונים נוספים חשובים בהרבה בהבנת עוצמות וכיווני הרווח ברוחות תיעול.

דמיינו לעצמכם ואדי המהווה את המעבר היחידי האפשרי עבור משב רוח כמתואר באיור.
רוח קלילה המנשבת ממזרח מתקרבת לאזור הכניסה לוואדי, ובהסתמך על חוק שימור המסה על מסת האוויר להאיץ על מנת לעבור במכשול כאשר המהירות המקסימלית תתקבל בחלק הצר ביותר של הוואדי.

במילים אחרות בדיוק אותה כמות המסה הנעה באיטיות בחלק הרחב של הוואדי תנוע במהירות בחלק הצר יותר, כשהאוויר ינוע אל אזור היציאה המתרחב הרוח תאט שוב.
על פי עקרון ברנולי לחץ האוויר צריך לרדת עם כיוון הזרימה כשמסת האוויר נעה מערבה ומאטה.

בפועל המצב שונה והרוח החזקה מתקבלת דווקא ביציאה מהמכשול.
ישנן מס' סיבות לכשל זה במודל: 
ראשית לא קיים בטבע מנגנון שיכול לתפקד "כמכסה קשיח" ולפיכך כשאוויר (בד"כ קר וצפוף באופן יחסי) נע לאזור הצר של הוואדי  "עומקה" של מסת האוויר גדל גידול זה יוצר אזור של לחץ אויר גבוה בקרבת מרכז הוואדי.
שנית באזור היציאה מהוואדי ההתרחבות העקבית במבנה הטופוגרפי גורמת לזרימה להתרחב במישור האופקי ולהצר במישור האנכי. היצרות זו יוצרת ירידה בלחץ האוויר המולידה גרדיינט לחץ באזור היציאה
במצב בו קיים אזור לחץ סינופטי גבוה בצד אחד של הוואדי ואזור לחץ נמוך בצדו האחר גרדיינט תנשב הרוח מהלחץ הגבוה לנמוך ותסייע להאיץ את הרוח באזור היציאה

על אף שהאפקט הוונטורי אינו בד"כ המנגנון המכני "השולט" בוואדיות או "מעברים טופוגרפיים" בסדר גודל של 10-100 ק"מ.

בוואדיות קטנים, באורך של מס' ק"מ או פחות, הוא יכול להיות מאוד דומיננטי. במקרים אלו התרומה של גרדיינט הלחץ הסינופטי או שינויים בגובה האוויר הקר במפלס הנמוך אינם כה חשובים.

בחלק הבא נבין מדוע רוחות תיעול הן בד"כ לא גיאוסטרופיות כך
שהזרם מאיץ עם כיוון הירידה בלחץ, בניגוד לזרימה הגיאוסטרופית
שמקבילה לאיזוברים ואנכית לגרדיינט הלחץ .

כמתואר ברוב ספרי התיאוריה ללא החיכוך של הטופוגרפיה רוחות קרקע צפויות להיות גיאוסטרופיות-מקבילות לאיזוברים ואנכיות לגרדיינט הלחץ. במצב זה יש איזון בין גרדיינט הלחץ המופנה ללחץ הנמוך וכוח קוריאוליס הפונה ימינה מכיוון הזרימה.

על מנת שתתקבל זרימה גיאוסטרופית במציאות נדרש יותר מחסרונו של חיכוך :
1- שינויים מינימליים בשדות הלחץ והרוח. 
2- שנתיב הרוח לא יהיה מפותל מידי – על מנת שכח קוריאוליס לא 	יהיה דומיננטי מידי.


במציאות אין מספיק זמן לרוח לאזן עצמה לגרדיינט הלחץ כך שלא נוצר איזון גיאוסטרופי של ממש.

Visibility was first defined for meteorological purposes as a quantity to be estimated by a human observer, and observations made in that way are widely used.
 However, the estimation of visibility is affected by many subjective and physical factors; the essential meteorological quantity, Which is the transparency of the atmosphere, can be measured objected, and is represented by the meteorological optical range (MOR).
MOR is defined as the distance where the intensity of a light beam has been attenuated to 5% of the original intensity.The meteorological optical range or MOR is expressed in meters or kilometers.

MOR can be measured by measuring the attenuation of light.
Attenuation is mainly caused by scattering, to a small degree also by absorption (in smoke, dust, …)

Traditionally RVR has been assessed by counting edge light lamps by the runway. The lamps are at 60 m distance from each other. At CAT I airport at least 14 lamps should be seen and 7 lamps at CAT II airport.

Pilots require 1-3 seconds to establish visual contact
To establish lateral position pilots required to see not less than three lights
To maintain lateral most pilots require to be able to see a lateral element of ground pattern
Vertical plane - see a point which has low apparent movement relative to the aircraft

Runway Visual Range (RVR) = Range over which the pilot on the center line of the runway can see:
                 1. Runway markings, or	
                 2. Edge lights of the runway, or	
           3. Center line lights. 
The maximum RVR reading is 2,000 meters or 6,000 feet, above which it is not significant and thus does not need to be reported.

Three basic portions of runway - the touchdown zone (TDZ), the mid-runway portion (MID) and the rollout portion or stop end
RVRs are provided in METARs and are transmitted by air traffic controllers to aircraft making approaches to allow pilots to assess whether it is prudent and legal to make an approach.

RVR assessment calculation follows Allard’s law 
        (V = e-σ*V/0.00336) which takes into account :
              1.Visibility (m)
              2.Background luminance (cd/m2)
              3.Airfield lighting intensity percentage
              4.Airfield lighting characteristics (cd)
Where V is the visibility and σ is the extinction coefficient. 
Most applications will use only the Koschmieder's (V = 3/σ) formula
For RVR calculations 5 m is used as the average eye level of a pilot in an aircraft.

In these instruments, a light beam is concentrated on a small volume of air in front of the transmitter, the receiver being located in the same housing and below the light source where it receives the light back scattered by the volume of air sample.

The instruments, comprise a transmitter and a receiver, the angle between the beam being 20 to 50°. Another arrangement involves placing either a single diaphragm half-way between a transmitter and a receiver or two diaphragms each a short distance from either a transmitter or receiver.

Transmissometer is an instrument for measuring the extinction coefficient of the atmosphere, and for the determination of visual range. 
It operates by sending a narrow, collimated beam of energy (usually a laser) through the propagation medium. 
A narrow field of view receiver at the designated measurement distance determines how much energy is arriving at the detector, and determines the path transmission and/or extinction coefficient.

Atmospheric extinction is wavelength dependent phenomenon, but the most common wavelength in use for transmissometers is 550 nm, which is right in the middle of the visible waveband, and allows a good approximation of visual range.
Using an infra-red light source and intelligent sensing technology the measurements are unaffected by other light-sources.
